properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by Anthony, in his words: "I'm leaning to the async shape option."

This settles the half `dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types` left open. That decision chose option A (a skill the user types) as a FIRST STEP and named option C — a hook deciding WHEN — as the destination. It decided WHO triggers capture. This decides the SHAPE of the hook that C needs, which was left open on a cost the earlier decision never measured.

═══ THE CONSTRAINT THAT FORCED THE CHOICE ═══

The shared server answers stateless MCP over the URL in `.reflow2/graph.server.json`, so the hook CAN read the graph. (The comment in `loop_nudge.py` saying it cannot — "the session's own server holds the single-writer lock" — was written before the shared server existed and is now false.) But measured live on this design: `loop_status` is 22.6s, repeatably, and `since_export: true` takes it to 37.5s. A Stop hook that blocks for 23 seconds is worse than no hook.

Two shapes were on the table:
  • A CHEAPER CALL — ask something the server answers fast (`claim_report` is 0.04s). Rejected: the cheap calls do not answer the question. Nothing under a second says what a session left uncaptured.
  • THE ASYNC SHAPE — ask at one stop, answer at a later one. CHOSEN.

═══ WHAT THIS DECIDES ═══

The Stop hook SPAWNS a detached probe and returns immediately, never waiting. The probe's answer lands in a per-session file. A LATER Stop in the same session reads it and speaks. A session stops once per TURN, not once per session, so on any session longer than a couple of turns the answer arrives while the agent is still alive and can act on it. When a session ends before its answer lands, the next SessionStart reports it instead — which is the fallback, not the design.

═══ THE TRIGGER IS A DELTA, NOT A LEVEL — and this is the load-bearing restraint ═══

The graph's standing debt on this design is 7 unsurfaced gaps and 60 structural defects, and both have stood for weeks. A nudge that fires on a LEVEL would fire on every session forever and would be a nag rather than a trigger — the fire-on-correct-work failure `ver:skill-triggers` names.

So the probe records a BASELINE at SessionStart and fires only where a later probe shows a count this session RAISED. "This session took open gaps from 7 to 10 and never put the three new ones to the user" is a fact about the session. "There are 10 open gaps" is not.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE ═══
  • It does not amend `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`. That requirement still says the user must never be the trigger, and this is the first mechanism that does not make him one — but the capture-session skill it complements is still typed by hand.
  • It does not make the graph able to see the transcript. The hook asks what the GRAPH says changed, never what the conversation held.
  • `since_export` is deliberately NOT in the probe: 15 extra seconds for a signal the delta already carries.
properties.name: DECIDED — the Stop hook asks the graph ASYNCHRONOUSLY: it fires the question at one stop and reports the answer at a later one
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own node rather than folded into dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types because the two answer different questions: that one settles WHO triggers capture (the user, as a first step), this settles HOW the hook half can ask at all. The cost measurement is the whole argument and would otherwise be lost — the obvious reading, "a hook cannot read the graph", was true when the comment was written and is false now, while the real obstacle is 22.6 seconds, a different problem with a different answer. A later session that rediscovers the HTTP mechanism and concludes the hook can simply call loop_status will ship a 23-second block.
